STATUS AND SCOPE This source proves a complete-record comparison for arbitrary measurable DETERMINISTIC moving linear probes and deterministic hidden controls, with fixed total observation energy. No bound on sensor variation, switching count, number of visited regions, or total number of regions is required. Independent public coins may choose the entire schedules before observation. The proof uses an exact Gaussian likelihood-overlap identity and the held dimension-independent polynomial endpoint theorem. It takes Brownian cancellation before absolute polynomial coefficients. The resulting explicit bound is O(n^(-1/2)) at fixed physical budgets, uniformly over arbitrary finite region count. Its constants are conservative; no useful finite-size threshold or numerical advantage is inferred. The source does NOT prove the corresponding arbitrary predictable-feedback moving-probe theorem. Section 6 gives the exact obstacle to that inference, including a bounded two-stage counterexample to the needed naive overlap identity. This counterexample refutes an argument, not the desired theorem. Novelty and practical advantage remain UNKNOWN. 1. There are K finite regions with n spins each; K may grow arbitrarily with n. Within each region the n-site internal balanced kernels have a common gap. Cross-site donor kernels are balanced, but coarse migration need only have outgoing row sums at most Lambda. The regional clock is n, not K n. The target initial JOINT regional law is the exact pushforward of the microscopic initial law. Arbitrary microscopic initial correlations are permitted. All public hidden controls on [0,T], including internal responses, are deterministic admitted profiles in this theorem. Their path variation can be arbitrary. The source's endpoint bound is uniform over all such profiles and all admitted response restarts. The backward target semigroup contracts the coefficient-l1 norm of allele polynomials p_a=(x_a+1)/2 and preserves degree. For every degree-D polynomial F with coefficient norm C and every interval of length h<=T, the held input is |E_micro F(p_end)-E_target F(P_end)| <= C E_D(n,h). With the nonnegative constants v,f,q_*,A,G from the held source, C_D=(2Lambda+A)T_2+2A T_3+(A+G)T_4/2, E_D(n,h) =(1/2){vT_2+h[fT_2+vC_D+q_*T_3]} +(h/n)[2Lambda T_2+(G/3)T_3]. (1.2) This expression is nondecreasing in h. At fixed physical budgets, v,f,q_*=O(n^(-1/2)), A,G=O(1). Also E_0=E_1=0 exactly. The endpoint constants are imported at this precise scope, not re-proved here. Let deterministic measurable weights w(t) in R^K satisfy sum_a |w_a(t)|<=1 almost everywhere. Let H:[0,T]->R be deterministic measurable with integral H_t^2 dt<=Gamma. (1.3) The two signals are Z_t^n=sum_a w_a(t)x_a^n(t), Z_t=sum_a w_a(t)X_a(t), and the actual observation models are dY_t=H_t Z_t^n dt+dW_t, dY_t=H_t Z_t dt+dW_t. (1.4) The hidden driving noises and observation Brownian motion are independent. Use predictable representatives of the bounded signals; changing values at the hidden chain's jump instants has no effect on these dt-based observations. The weights may vary with n and K and need not have bounded total variation. 2. COMPLETE-RECORD CERTIFICATE Denote the entire record laws on C([0,T]) by P_n and P. Then TV(P_n,P) <= min{1, (1/2)[sum_(d>=1) Gamma^d/d! min{2, d 3^d E_d(n,T)}^2]^(1/2)} <= min{1, (1/2)[sum_(d>=1) (9Gamma)^d/d! d^2 E_d(n,T)^2]^(1/2)}. (2.1) The d=1 term is zero because E_1=0. For Gamma=0 both record laws are the same Wiener law and the right side is interpreted as zero. The second series in (2.1) is finite. Its summand is a degree-at-most-ten polynomial in d times (9Gamma)^d/d!, so it can also be evaluated as a finite linear combination of Touchard polynomials. No observation time grid or likelihood-degree truncation is used in the theorem. A completely explicit coarse finite expression follows. Define B_n(T)=(v+Tf)/8 +T v[(Lambda+A)/4+(A+G)/64] +T q_*/16+(T/n)[Lambda/2+G/24], (2.2) and the polynomial T10(z)=z+511z^2+9330z^3+34105z^4+42525z^5 +22827z^6+5880z^7+750z^8+45z^9+z^10. Then TV(P_n,P) <=min{1, [B_n(T)/2] sqrt(exp(9Gamma) T10(9Gamma))}. (2.3) Indeed E_d(n,T)<=B_n(T)d^4 for integers d>=1, using T_2<=d^2/4, T_3<=d^3/8, T_4<=d^4/16. The identity sum_(d>=0) d^10 z^d/d! = exp(z) T10(z) follows by applying (z d/dz)^10 to exp(z), or by the elementary Stirling recurrence. Thus (2.3) is O(n^(-1/2)) for fixed T,Gamma and physical budgets, uniformly over K and every precommitted sensor/control schedule described above. This rate has no sensor variation or visited-region factor. 3. MULTITIME MOMENT INPUT FOR DIFFERENT OBSERVABLES AT EVERY TIME For deterministic times t_1,...,t_d, let F_j(p)=sum_a w_a(t_j)(2p_a-1). Then |F_j|<=1 and ||F_j||_coef<=3, regardless of K or the weights' signs. Sort the times and include the initial time zero. Repeated times cause no problem: multiply their polynomial factors at that state. Starting at the last time, multiply by the current F_j and propagate with the target backward transition. Degree never exceeds d; coefficient norm never exceeds 3^d. The usual discrete conditional-expectation telescope uses the actual full microscopic state at every restart. One can either expand every factor into allele monomials, whose past products lie in [0,1], or use |F_j|<=1 together with the coefficient bound on each remaining continuation. Applying (1.1) to each gap gives |E prod_(j=1)^d Z^n_(t_j)-E prod_(j=1)^d Z_(t_j)| <=3^d sum_(j=1)^d E_d(n,t_j-t_(j-1)) <=d 3^d E_d(n,T). For d=1 both systems' first moments solve the same deterministic linear migration law, so the difference is exactly zero, as (3.1) records. This is a moment statement for a different linear observable at every time. It does not freeze a sensor schedule or assert a modulus for a rapidly moving scalar Z_t. Such a modulus is neither assumed nor needed below. 4. EXACT LIKELIHOOD OVERLAP: PROOF OF (2.1) Let W denote Wiener measure on the observation path. For a deterministic u in L2([0,T]), define L_u(Y)=exp{integral u_t dY_t-(1/2)||u||_2^2}. It is a normalized density. For deterministic u,v the Gaussian exponential identity is E_W[L_u L_v]=exp(<u,v>_L2). (4.1) For example L_u L_v=exp(<u,v>) L_(u+v), whose latter factor has expectation one. This identity first follows for step functions from independent normal increments and then extends in L2 by Gaussian convergence. Under the reference construction, the complete hidden path is independent of Y because every command and the observation schedule is precommitted. Conditional on that hidden path, u_t=H_t Z_t is deterministic for purposes of Wiener integration and ||u||_2^2<=Gamma. Therefore the record density is ell_n(Y)=E_hidden L_(H Z^n)(Y), ell(Y)=E_hidden L_(H Z)(Y). Both are normalized and in L2(W), with squared norms at most exp(Gamma). Introduce independent copies of each hidden signal for their quadratic overlaps. Equation (4.1) gives ||ell_n-ell||_L2(W)^2 = E exp(<u_n,u_n'>)+E exp(<u,u'>) -2E exp(<u_n,u>). (4.2) All inner products have absolute value at most Gamma. Hence Taylor expansion of every exponential and every Fubini exchange are justified by the common bound exp(Gamma). For d>=0, expand <u,v>^d as an integral over [0,T]^d. Independence of the two hidden copies factors its expectation. Combining the three terms gives the NONNEGATIVE exact identity ||ell_n-ell||_2^2 =sum_(d>=0) (1/d!) integral_[0,T]^d [ E prod_j u_n(t_j)-E prod_j u(t_j) ]^2 dt_1...dt_d. (4.3) The d=0 term is zero. Since H is deterministic, its factors separate from the hidden moments. Equations (3.1) and integral H^2<=Gamma give the first series in (2.1). Dropping the minimum gives the second. Finally TV(P_n,P)=(1/2)||ell_n-ell||_L1(W) <=(1/2)||ell_n-ell||_L2(W). This proves the complete continuous-record assertion. The proof is the Wiener-chaos norm identity written directly as a two-replica Gaussian overlap; no chaos theorem beyond the elementary calculation is imported. 5. PUBLIC COINS, COSTS, AND THE REPRESENTATION CHANGE The entire construction can be conditioned on declared independent public coins that select the schedules before observation. Initial hidden laws may depend on those coins provided their conditional joint initialization agrees. The deterministic certificate is uniform, so integrating proves exactly the same bound for the JOINT output (coins, complete record). The schedules can be complicated supplied functions. Their description, evaluation, controller clock, graph rows, all internal response coordinates, initial joint law, and arithmetic precision remain charged. This theorem does not reduce the K-dimensional physical field to a finite posterior or give an efficient sampler/evaluator for arbitrary schedules. It supplies an operational record comparison, not an implementation complexity theorem. The representation change is substantive. For example, visiting K static coordinates on disjoint windows of equal observation energy Gamma/K gives independent reference coefficients b_i~N(0,Gamma/K). Their expected l1 norm is sqrt(2Gamma K/pi). Thus a proof that first conditions on the reference record and then bounds all linear polynomial coefficients absolutely can lose uniformity even for deterministic sensors. Equation (4.3) retains the Gaussian cancellations and avoids that false obstruction completely. This example is not a lower bound on record approximation or state memory. The present theorem proves the relevant record comparison despite that coefficient-l1 growth. 6. WHY THIS DOES NOT YET PROVE ARBITRARY MOVING-PROBE FEEDBACK For predictable record-dependent weights, H, or hidden controls, the same bounded-energy stochastic exponentials remain normalized. But the step from (4.1) to (4.2) is no longer valid: after fixing a hidden primitive path, the signal can still depend on Y. With hidden feedback, even the hidden path itself depends on Y under the canonical reference construction. The true product identity for two adapted signal processes u,v is L_u L_v=mathcal E(integral (u+v)dY)_T exp(integral uv dt). (6.1) The second factor is generally random and correlated with the exponential martingale. Its expectation is taken under the TWO-REPLICA tilted law, not under the original Wiener law. In particular, one cannot use (4.3) with random future-record-dependent moment kernels and retain orthogonality. An exact two-stage bounded example makes the failure visible. Let the two unit-interval Wiener increments be Z1,Z2, independent N(0,1). A predictable signal is a on the first interval and b 1_{Z1>0} on the second. It can be implemented with deterministic H=(a,b), a constant hidden state equal to one, and an adaptive weight in [0,1]. Its total energy is at most a^2+b^2. The likelihood is L=exp(a Z1-a^2/2) exp(b 1_{Z1>0} Z2-b^2 1_{Z1>0}/2). Writing Phi for the standard normal distribution function, exact Gaussian integration gives E_W L^2=exp(a^2)[1+(exp(b^2)-1)Phi(2a)], whereas E_W exp(integral u^2dt) =exp(a^2)[1+(exp(b^2)-1)/2]. (6.2) These differ when a,b are nonzero. Hence replacing the adapted overlap by an untilted overlap is false even with one hidden coordinate and bounded total energy. This is not a counterexample to a dimension-free feedback record theorem; it only blocks the naive extension of this proof. Likewise the existing terminal-zero microscopic corrector depends on the future deterministic command profile. After substituting a feedback profile, that corrector is generally not adapted. It cannot be inserted into an original causal Itô argument without a separately proved representation. The deterministic conditional-profile use in (3.1) is legitimate; an anticipating stochastic product rule is not. The remaining precise interface is a predictable stochastic observable algebra estimate: it must control the two-replica tilted expectations or an adapted likelihood/duality expansion in terms of the uniform degree-D moment certificates, while retaining Brownian cancellation before summing absolute spatial coefficients. A bound on expected coefficient-l1 mass alone cannot provide that interface, as Section 5's deterministic example already shows. No such adapted estimate is claimed here. Nor is its impossibility claimed. 7. RECEIPT AND CONTINUATION The concrete restricted objective is complete: arbitrary precommitted sensor motion now has a dimension-free full-record theorem and an explicit O(n^(-1/2)) certificate. It removes the fixed spatial-sensor restriction for this class without a visit-count or time-variation requirement. The earlier fixed-sensor theorem still covers its separately stated arbitrary feedback class; neither theorem silently contains the other's entire control class. Precommitted Moving Linear Probe Record Theorem
PRECOMMITTED MOVING LINEAR PROBES: A DIMENSION-FREE COMPLETE-RECORD THEOREM

Private ASTRA-FRESH-20261023 / P1 / construction_attack.
New source; all previously held proofs remain unchanged.

STATUS AND SCOPE

This source proves a complete-record comparison for arbitrary measurable
DETERMINISTIC moving linear probes and deterministic hidden controls, with
fixed total observation energy. No bound on sensor variation, switching
count, number of visited regions, or total number of regions is required.
Independent public coins may choose the entire schedules before observation.

The proof uses an exact Gaussian likelihood-overlap identity and the held
dimension-independent polynomial endpoint theorem. It takes Brownian
cancellation before absolute polynomial coefficients. The resulting explicit
bound is O(n^(-1/2)) at fixed physical budgets, uniformly over arbitrary finite
region count. Its constants are conservative; no useful finite-size threshold
or numerical advantage is inferred.

The source does NOT prove the corresponding arbitrary predictable-feedback
moving-probe theorem. Section 6 gives the exact obstacle to that inference,
including a bounded two-stage counterexample to the needed naive overlap
identity. This counterexample refutes an argument, not the desired theorem.
Novelty and practical advantage remain UNKNOWN.

1. INPUTS AND NOTATION

The microscopic many-region model and target field are exactly those in the
held endpoint source

 agents/many_region_polynomial/
 DIMENSION_INDEPENDENT_REGIONAL_POLYNOMIAL_ENDPOINT_THEOREM.txt
 SHA256 088af9e2dc49c0484d1c7d68ad25f9c43f19576d1d5aabb68d42d7926dc9b7a8.

There are K finite regions with n spins each; K may grow arbitrarily with n.
Within each region the n-site internal balanced kernels have a common gap.
Cross-site donor kernels are balanced, but coarse migration need only have
outgoing row sums at most Lambda. The regional clock is n, not K n. The
target initial JOINT regional law is the exact pushforward of the microscopic
initial law. Arbitrary microscopic initial correlations are permitted.

All public hidden controls on [0,T], including internal responses, are
deterministic admitted profiles in this theorem. Their path variation can be
arbitrary. The source's endpoint bound is uniform over all such profiles and
all admitted response restarts. The backward target semigroup contracts the
coefficient-l1 norm of allele polynomials p_a=(x_a+1)/2 and preserves degree.

For every degree-D polynomial F with coefficient norm C and every interval
of length h<=T, the held input is

 |E_micro F(p_end)-E_target F(P_end)| <= C E_D(n,h).     (1.1)

It applies from every microscopic state and its matching regional vector.
The same actual public response context is retained at interval boundaries.
Write T_r(D)=(D)_r/2^r, with T_r=0 for D<r. With the nonnegative constants
v,f,q_*,A,G from the held source,

 C_D=(2Lambda+A)T_2+2A T_3+(A+G)T_4/2,

 E_D(n,h)
  =(1/2){vT_2+h[fT_2+vC_D+q_*T_3]}
                  +(h/n)[2Lambda T_2+(G/3)T_3].       (1.2)

This expression is nondecreasing in h. At fixed physical budgets,
v,f,q_*=O(n^(-1/2)), A,G=O(1). Also E_0=E_1=0 exactly.
The endpoint constants are imported at this precise scope, not re-proved here.

Let deterministic measurable weights w(t) in R^K satisfy

              sum_a |w_a(t)|<=1 almost everywhere.

Let H:[0,T]->R be deterministic measurable with

                    integral H_t^2 dt<=Gamma.         (1.3)

The two signals are

 Z_t^n=sum_a w_a(t)x_a^n(t),   Z_t=sum_a w_a(t)X_a(t),

and the actual observation models are

                dY_t=H_t Z_t^n dt+dW_t,
                dY_t=H_t Z_t dt+dW_t.                (1.4)

The hidden driving noises and observation Brownian motion are independent.
Use predictable representatives of the bounded signals; changing values at
the hidden chain's jump instants has no effect on these dt-based observations.
The weights may vary with n and K and need not have bounded total variation.

2. COMPLETE-RECORD CERTIFICATE

Denote the entire record laws on C([0,T]) by P_n and P. Then

 TV(P_n,P)
 <= min{1, (1/2)[sum_(d>=1) Gamma^d/d!
                min{2, d 3^d E_d(n,T)}^2]^(1/2)}
 <= min{1, (1/2)[sum_(d>=1) (9Gamma)^d/d!
                         d^2 E_d(n,T)^2]^(1/2)}.      (2.1)

The d=1 term is zero because E_1=0. For Gamma=0 both record laws are the
same Wiener law and the right side is interpreted as zero.

The second series in (2.1) is finite. Its summand is a degree-at-most-ten
polynomial in d times (9Gamma)^d/d!, so it can also be evaluated as a finite
linear combination of Touchard polynomials. No observation time grid or
likelihood-degree truncation is used in the theorem.

A completely explicit coarse finite expression follows. Define

 B_n(T)=(v+Tf)/8
       +T v[(Lambda+A)/4+(A+G)/64]
       +T q_*/16+(T/n)[Lambda/2+G/24],                (2.2)

 and the polynomial

 T10(z)=z+511z^2+9330z^3+34105z^4+42525z^5
          +22827z^6+5880z^7+750z^8+45z^9+z^10.

Then

 TV(P_n,P)
  <=min{1, [B_n(T)/2] sqrt(exp(9Gamma) T10(9Gamma))}. (2.3)

Indeed E_d(n,T)<=B_n(T)d^4 for integers d>=1, using
T_2<=d^2/4, T_3<=d^3/8, T_4<=d^4/16. The identity

 sum_(d>=0) d^10 z^d/d! = exp(z) T10(z)

follows by applying (z d/dz)^10 to exp(z), or by the elementary Stirling
recurrence. Thus (2.3) is O(n^(-1/2)) for fixed T,Gamma and physical budgets,
uniformly over K and every precommitted sensor/control schedule described
above. This rate has no sensor variation or visited-region factor.

3. MULTITIME MOMENT INPUT FOR DIFFERENT OBSERVABLES AT EVERY TIME

For deterministic times t_1,...,t_d, let

 F_j(p)=sum_a w_a(t_j)(2p_a-1).

Then |F_j|<=1 and ||F_j||_coef<=3, regardless of K or the weights' signs.
Sort the times and include the initial time zero. Repeated times cause no
problem: multiply their polynomial factors at that state. Starting at the
last time, multiply by the current F_j and propagate with the target backward
transition. Degree never exceeds d; coefficient norm never exceeds 3^d.

The usual discrete conditional-expectation telescope uses the actual full
microscopic state at every restart. One can either expand every factor into
allele monomials, whose past products lie in [0,1], or use |F_j|<=1 together
with the coefficient bound on each remaining continuation. Applying (1.1)
to each gap gives

 |E prod_(j=1)^d Z^n_(t_j)-E prod_(j=1)^d Z_(t_j)|
       <=3^d sum_(j=1)^d E_d(n,t_j-t_(j-1))
       <=d 3^d E_d(n,T).                              (3.1)

Here the first gap from zero to the earliest observation time is included;
there are at most d transitions. The trivial bound is also at most 2.
For d=1 both systems' first moments solve the same deterministic linear
migration law, so the difference is exactly zero, as (3.1) records.

This is a moment statement for a different linear observable at every time.
It does not freeze a sensor schedule or assert a modulus for a rapidly
moving scalar Z_t. Such a modulus is neither assumed nor needed below.

4. EXACT LIKELIHOOD OVERLAP: PROOF OF (2.1)

Let W denote Wiener measure on the observation path. For a deterministic
u in L2([0,T]), define

 L_u(Y)=exp{integral u_t dY_t-(1/2)||u||_2^2}.

It is a normalized density. For deterministic u,v the Gaussian exponential
identity is

       E_W[L_u L_v]=exp(<u,v>_L2).                    (4.1)

For example L_u L_v=exp(<u,v>) L_(u+v), whose latter factor has expectation
one. This identity first follows for step functions from independent normal
increments and then extends in L2 by Gaussian convergence.

Under the reference construction, the complete hidden path is independent
of Y because every command and the observation schedule is precommitted.
Conditional on that hidden path, u_t=H_t Z_t is deterministic for purposes
of Wiener integration and ||u||_2^2<=Gamma. Therefore the record density is

 ell_n(Y)=E_hidden L_(H Z^n)(Y),
 ell(Y)=E_hidden L_(H Z)(Y).

Both are normalized and in L2(W), with squared norms at most exp(Gamma).
Introduce independent copies of each hidden signal for their quadratic
overlaps. Equation (4.1) gives

 ||ell_n-ell||_L2(W)^2
  = E exp(<u_n,u_n'>)+E exp(<u,u'>)
                              -2E exp(<u_n,u>).       (4.2)

All inner products have absolute value at most Gamma. Hence Taylor
expansion of every exponential and every Fubini exchange are justified by
the common bound exp(Gamma). For d>=0, expand <u,v>^d as an integral over
[0,T]^d. Independence of the two hidden copies factors its expectation.
Combining the three terms gives the NONNEGATIVE exact identity

 ||ell_n-ell||_2^2
   =sum_(d>=0) (1/d!) integral_[0,T]^d
       [ E prod_j u_n(t_j)-E prod_j u(t_j) ]^2 dt_1...dt_d.
                                                        (4.3)

The d=0 term is zero. Since H is deterministic, its factors separate from
the hidden moments. Equations (3.1) and integral H^2<=Gamma give the first
series in (2.1). Dropping the minimum gives the second. Finally

 TV(P_n,P)=(1/2)||ell_n-ell||_L1(W)
                           <=(1/2)||ell_n-ell||_L2(W).

This proves the complete continuous-record assertion. The proof is the
Wiener-chaos norm identity written directly as a two-replica Gaussian
overlap; no chaos theorem beyond the elementary calculation is imported.

5. PUBLIC COINS, COSTS, AND THE REPRESENTATION CHANGE

The entire construction can be conditioned on declared independent public
coins that select the schedules before observation. Initial hidden laws may
depend on those coins provided their conditional joint initialization agrees.
The deterministic certificate is uniform, so integrating proves exactly the
same bound for the JOINT output (coins, complete record).

The schedules can be complicated supplied functions. Their description,
evaluation, controller clock, graph rows, all internal response coordinates,
initial joint law, and arithmetic precision remain charged. This theorem
does not reduce the K-dimensional physical field to a finite posterior or
give an efficient sampler/evaluator for arbitrary schedules. It supplies an
operational record comparison, not an implementation complexity theorem.

The representation change is substantive. For example, visiting K static
coordinates on disjoint windows of equal observation energy Gamma/K gives
independent reference coefficients b_i~N(0,Gamma/K). Their expected l1 norm
is sqrt(2Gamma K/pi). Thus a proof that first conditions on the reference
record and then bounds all linear polynomial coefficients absolutely can
lose uniformity even for deterministic sensors. Equation (4.3) retains the
Gaussian cancellations and avoids that false obstruction completely.

This example is not a lower bound on record approximation or state memory.
The present theorem proves the relevant record comparison despite that
coefficient-l1 growth.

6. WHY THIS DOES NOT YET PROVE ARBITRARY MOVING-PROBE FEEDBACK

For predictable record-dependent weights, H, or hidden controls, the same
bounded-energy stochastic exponentials remain normalized. But the step
from (4.1) to (4.2) is no longer valid: after fixing a hidden primitive path,
the signal can still depend on Y. With hidden feedback, even the hidden path
itself depends on Y under the canonical reference construction.

The true product identity for two adapted signal processes u,v is

 L_u L_v=mathcal E(integral (u+v)dY)_T
                                      exp(integral uv dt). (6.1)

The second factor is generally random and correlated with the exponential
martingale. Its expectation is taken under the TWO-REPLICA tilted law, not
under the original Wiener law. In particular, one cannot use (4.3) with
random future-record-dependent moment kernels and retain orthogonality.

An exact two-stage bounded example makes the failure visible. Let the two
unit-interval Wiener increments be Z1,Z2, independent N(0,1). A predictable
signal is a on the first interval and b 1_{Z1>0} on the second. It can be
implemented with deterministic H=(a,b), a constant hidden state equal to
one, and an adaptive weight in [0,1]. Its total energy is at most a^2+b^2.
The likelihood is

 L=exp(a Z1-a^2/2)
       exp(b 1_{Z1>0} Z2-b^2 1_{Z1>0}/2).

Writing Phi for the standard normal distribution function, exact Gaussian
integration gives

 E_W L^2=exp(a^2)[1+(exp(b^2)-1)Phi(2a)],

 whereas

 E_W exp(integral u^2dt)
             =exp(a^2)[1+(exp(b^2)-1)/2].             (6.2)

These differ when a,b are nonzero. Hence replacing the adapted overlap by
an untilted overlap is false even with one hidden coordinate and bounded
total energy. This is not a counterexample to a dimension-free feedback
record theorem; it only blocks the naive extension of this proof.

Likewise the existing terminal-zero microscopic corrector depends on the
future deterministic command profile. After substituting a feedback profile,
that corrector is generally not adapted. It cannot be inserted into an
original causal Itô argument without a separately proved representation.
The deterministic conditional-profile use in (3.1) is legitimate; an
anticipating stochastic product rule is not.

The remaining precise interface is a predictable stochastic observable
algebra estimate: it must control the two-replica tilted expectations or an
adapted likelihood/duality expansion in terms of the uniform degree-D moment
certificates, while retaining Brownian cancellation before summing absolute
spatial coefficients. A bound on expected coefficient-l1 mass alone cannot
provide that interface, as Section 5's deterministic example already shows.
No such adapted estimate is claimed here. Nor is its impossibility claimed.

7. RECEIPT AND CONTINUATION

The concrete restricted objective is complete: arbitrary precommitted
sensor motion now has a dimension-free full-record theorem and an explicit
O(n^(-1/2)) certificate. It removes the fixed spatial-sensor restriction for
this class without a visit-count or time-variation requirement. The earlier
fixed-sensor theorem still covers its separately stated arbitrary feedback
class; neither theorem silently contains the other's entire control class.

Precommitted Moving Linear Probe Record Theorem PRECOMMITTED MOVING LINEAR PROBES: A DIMENSION-FREE COMPLETE-RECORD THEOREM

Private ASTRA-FRESH-20261023 / P1 / construction_attack.
New source; all previously held proofs remain unchanged.

STATUS AND SCOPE

This source proves a complete-record comparison for arbitrary measurable
DETERMINISTIC moving linear probes and deterministic hidden controls, with
fixed total observation energy. No bound on sensor variation, switching
count, number of visited regions, or total number of regions is required.
Independent public coins may choose the entire schedules before observation.

The proof uses an exact Gaussian likelihood-overlap identity and the held
dimension-independent polynomial endpoint theorem. It takes Brownian
cancellation before absolute polynomial coefficients. The resulting explicit
bound is O(n^(-1/2)) at fixed physical budgets, uniformly over arbitrary finite
region count. Its constants are conservative; no useful finite-size threshold
or numerical advantage is inferred.

The source does NOT prove the corresponding arbitrary predictable-feedback
moving-probe theorem. Section 6 gives the exact obstacle to that inference,
including a bounded two-stage counterexample to the needed naive overlap
identity. This counterexample refutes an argument, not the desired theorem.
Novelty and practical advantage remain UNKNOWN.

1. INPUTS AND NOTATION

The microscopic many-region model and target field are exactly those in the
held endpoint source

 agents/many_region_polynomial/
 DIMENSION_INDEPENDENT_REGIONAL_POLYNOMIAL_ENDPOINT_THEOREM.txt
 SHA256 088af9e2dc49c0484d1c7d68ad25f9c43f19576d1d5aabb68d42d7926dc9b7a8.

There are K finite regions with n spins each; K may grow arbitrarily with n.
Within each region the n-site internal balanced kernels have a common gap.
Cross-site donor kernels are balanced, but coarse migration need only have
outgoing row sums at most Lambda. The regional clock is n, not K n. The
target initial JOINT regional law is the exact pushforward of the microscopic
initial law. Arbitrary microscopic initial correlations are permitted.

All public hidden controls on [0,T], including internal responses, are
deterministic admitted profiles in this theorem. Their path variation can be
arbitrary. The source's endpoint bound is uniform over all such profiles and
all admitted response restarts. The backward target semigroup contracts the
coefficient-l1 norm of allele polynomials p_a=(x_a+1)/2 and preserves degree.

For every degree-D polynomial F with coefficient norm C and every interval
of length h<=T, the held input is

 |E_micro F(p_end)-E_target F(P_end)| <= C E_D(n,h).     (1.1)

It applies from every microscopic state and its matching regional vector.
The same actual public response context is retained at interval boundaries.
Write T_r(D)=(D)_r/2^r, with T_r=0 for D<r. With the nonnegative constants
v,f,q_*,A,G from the held source,

 C_D=(2Lambda+A)T_2+2A T_3+(A+G)T_4/2,

 E_D(n,h)
  =(1/2){vT_2+h[fT_2+vC_D+q_*T_3]}
                  +(h/n)[2Lambda T_2+(G/3)T_3].       (1.2)

This expression is nondecreasing in h. At fixed physical budgets,
v,f,q_*=O(n^(-1/2)), A,G=O(1). Also E_0=E_1=0 exactly.
The endpoint constants are imported at this precise scope, not re-proved here.

Let deterministic measurable weights w(t) in R^K satisfy

              sum_a |w_a(t)|<=1 almost everywhere.

Let H:[0,T]->R be deterministic measurable with

                    integral H_t^2 dt<=Gamma.         (1.3)

The two signals are

 Z_t^n=sum_a w_a(t)x_a^n(t),   Z_t=sum_a w_a(t)X_a(t),

and the actual observation models are

                dY_t=H_t Z_t^n dt+dW_t,
                dY_t=H_t Z_t dt+dW_t.                (1.4)

The hidden driving noises and observation Brownian motion are independent.
Use predictable representatives of the bounded signals; changing values at
the hidden chain's jump instants has no effect on these dt-based observations.
The weights may vary with n and K and need not have bounded total variation.

2. COMPLETE-RECORD CERTIFICATE

Denote the entire record laws on C([0,T]) by P_n and P. Then

 TV(P_n,P)
 <= min{1, (1/2)[sum_(d>=1) Gamma^d/d!
                min{2, d 3^d E_d(n,T)}^2]^(1/2)}
 <= min{1, (1/2)[sum_(d>=1) (9Gamma)^d/d!
                         d^2 E_d(n,T)^2]^(1/2)}.      (2.1)

The d=1 term is zero because E_1=0. For Gamma=0 both record laws are the
same Wiener law and the right side is interpreted as zero.

The second series in (2.1) is finite. Its summand is a degree-at-most-ten
polynomial in d times (9Gamma)^d/d!, so it can also be evaluated as a finite
linear combination of Touchard polynomials. No observation time grid or
likelihood-degree truncation is used in the theorem.

A completely explicit coarse finite expression follows. Define

 B_n(T)=(v+Tf)/8
       +T v[(Lambda+A)/4+(A+G)/64]
       +T q_*/16+(T/n)[Lambda/2+G/24],                (2.2)

 and the polynomial

 T10(z)=z+511z^2+9330z^3+34105z^4+42525z^5
          +22827z^6+5880z^7+750z^8+45z^9+z^10.

Then

 TV(P_n,P)
  <=min{1, [B_n(T)/2] sqrt(exp(9Gamma) T10(9Gamma))}. (2.3)

Indeed E_d(n,T)<=B_n(T)d^4 for integers d>=1, using
T_2<=d^2/4, T_3<=d^3/8, T_4<=d^4/16. The identity

 sum_(d>=0) d^10 z^d/d! = exp(z) T10(z)

follows by applying (z d/dz)^10 to exp(z), or by the elementary Stirling
recurrence. Thus (2.3) is O(n^(-1/2)) for fixed T,Gamma and physical budgets,
uniformly over K and every precommitted sensor/control schedule described
above. This rate has no sensor variation or visited-region factor.

3. MULTITIME MOMENT INPUT FOR DIFFERENT OBSERVABLES AT EVERY TIME

For deterministic times t_1,...,t_d, let

 F_j(p)=sum_a w_a(t_j)(2p_a-1).

Then |F_j|<=1 and ||F_j||_coef<=3, regardless of K or the weights' signs.
Sort the times and include the initial time zero. Repeated times cause no
problem: multiply their polynomial factors at that state. Starting at the
last time, multiply by the current F_j and propagate with the target backward
transition. Degree never exceeds d; coefficient norm never exceeds 3^d.

The usual discrete conditional-expectation telescope uses the actual full
microscopic state at every restart. One can either expand every factor into
allele monomials, whose past products lie in [0,1], or use |F_j|<=1 together
with the coefficient bound on each remaining continuation. Applying (1.1)
to each gap gives

 |E prod_(j=1)^d Z^n_(t_j)-E prod_(j=1)^d Z_(t_j)|
       <=3^d sum_(j=1)^d E_d(n,t_j-t_(j-1))
       <=d 3^d E_d(n,T).                              (3.1)

Here the first gap from zero to the earliest observation time is included;
there are at most d transitions. The trivial bound is also at most 2.
For d=1 both systems' first moments solve the same deterministic linear
migration law, so the difference is exactly zero, as (3.1) records.

This is a moment statement for a different linear observable at every time.
It does not freeze a sensor schedule or assert a modulus for a rapidly
moving scalar Z_t. Such a modulus is neither assumed nor needed below.

4. EXACT LIKELIHOOD OVERLAP: PROOF OF (2.1)

Let W denote Wiener measure on the observation path. For a deterministic
u in L2([0,T]), define

 L_u(Y)=exp{integral u_t dY_t-(1/2)||u||_2^2}.

It is a normalized density. For deterministic u,v the Gaussian exponential
identity is

       E_W[L_u L_v]=exp(<u,v>_L2).                    (4.1)

For example L_u L_v=exp(<u,v>) L_(u+v), whose latter factor has expectation
one. This identity first follows for step functions from independent normal
increments and then extends in L2 by Gaussian convergence.

Under the reference construction, the complete hidden path is independent
of Y because every command and the observation schedule is precommitted.
Conditional on that hidden path, u_t=H_t Z_t is deterministic for purposes
of Wiener integration and ||u||_2^2<=Gamma. Therefore the record density is

 ell_n(Y)=E_hidden L_(H Z^n)(Y),
 ell(Y)=E_hidden L_(H Z)(Y).

Both are normalized and in L2(W), with squared norms at most exp(Gamma).
Introduce independent copies of each hidden signal for their quadratic
overlaps. Equation (4.1) gives

 ||ell_n-ell||_L2(W)^2
  = E exp(<u_n,u_n'>)+E exp(<u,u'>)
                              -2E exp(<u_n,u>).       (4.2)

All inner products have absolute value at most Gamma. Hence Taylor
expansion of every exponential and every Fubini exchange are justified by
the common bound exp(Gamma). For d>=0, expand <u,v>^d as an integral over
[0,T]^d. Independence of the two hidden copies factors its expectation.
Combining the three terms gives the NONNEGATIVE exact identity

 ||ell_n-ell||_2^2
   =sum_(d>=0) (1/d!) integral_[0,T]^d
       [ E prod_j u_n(t_j)-E prod_j u(t_j) ]^2 dt_1...dt_d.
                                                        (4.3)

The d=0 term is zero. Since H is deterministic, its factors separate from
the hidden moments. Equations (3.1) and integral H^2<=Gamma give the first
series in (2.1). Dropping the minimum gives the second. Finally

 TV(P_n,P)=(1/2)||ell_n-ell||_L1(W)
                           <=(1/2)||ell_n-ell||_L2(W).

This proves the complete continuous-record assertion. The proof is the
Wiener-chaos norm identity written directly as a two-replica Gaussian
overlap; no chaos theorem beyond the elementary calculation is imported.

5. PUBLIC COINS, COSTS, AND THE REPRESENTATION CHANGE

The entire construction can be conditioned on declared independent public
coins that select the schedules before observation. Initial hidden laws may
depend on those coins provided their conditional joint initialization agrees.
The deterministic certificate is uniform, so integrating proves exactly the
same bound for the JOINT output (coins, complete record).

The schedules can be complicated supplied functions. Their description,
evaluation, controller clock, graph rows, all internal response coordinates,
initial joint law, and arithmetic precision remain charged. This theorem
does not reduce the K-dimensional physical field to a finite posterior or
give an efficient sampler/evaluator for arbitrary schedules. It supplies an
operational record comparison, not an implementation complexity theorem.

The representation change is substantive. For example, visiting K static
coordinates on disjoint windows of equal observation energy Gamma/K gives
independent reference coefficients b_i~N(0,Gamma/K). Their expected l1 norm
is sqrt(2Gamma K/pi). Thus a proof that first conditions on the reference
record and then bounds all linear polynomial coefficients absolutely can
lose uniformity even for deterministic sensors. Equation (4.3) retains the
Gaussian cancellations and avoids that false obstruction completely.

This example is not a lower bound on record approximation or state memory.
The present theorem proves the relevant record comparison despite that
coefficient-l1 growth.

6. WHY THIS DOES NOT YET PROVE ARBITRARY MOVING-PROBE FEEDBACK

For predictable record-dependent weights, H, or hidden controls, the same
bounded-energy stochastic exponentials remain normalized. But the step
from (4.1) to (4.2) is no longer valid: after fixing a hidden primitive path,
the signal can still depend on Y. With hidden feedback, even the hidden path
itself depends on Y under the canonical reference construction.

The true product identity for two adapted signal processes u,v is

 L_u L_v=mathcal E(integral (u+v)dY)_T
                                      exp(integral uv dt). (6.1)

The second factor is generally random and correlated with the exponential
martingale. Its expectation is taken under the TWO-REPLICA tilted law, not
under the original Wiener law. In particular, one cannot use (4.3) with
random future-record-dependent moment kernels and retain orthogonality.

An exact two-stage bounded example makes the failure visible. Let the two
unit-interval Wiener increments be Z1,Z2, independent N(0,1). A predictable
signal is a on the first interval and b 1_{Z1>0} on the second. It can be
implemented with deterministic H=(a,b), a constant hidden state equal to
one, and an adaptive weight in [0,1]. Its total energy is at most a^2+b^2.
The likelihood is

 L=exp(a Z1-a^2/2)
       exp(b 1_{Z1>0} Z2-b^2 1_{Z1>0}/2).

Writing Phi for the standard normal distribution function, exact Gaussian
integration gives

 E_W L^2=exp(a^2)[1+(exp(b^2)-1)Phi(2a)],

 whereas

 E_W exp(integral u^2dt)
             =exp(a^2)[1+(exp(b^2)-1)/2].             (6.2)

These differ when a,b are nonzero. Hence replacing the adapted overlap by
an untilted overlap is false even with one hidden coordinate and bounded
total energy. This is not a counterexample to a dimension-free feedback
record theorem; it only blocks the naive extension of this proof.

Likewise the existing terminal-zero microscopic corrector depends on the
future deterministic command profile. After substituting a feedback profile,
that corrector is generally not adapted. It cannot be inserted into an
original causal Itô argument without a separately proved representation.
The deterministic conditional-profile use in (3.1) is legitimate; an
anticipating stochastic product rule is not.

The remaining precise interface is a predictable stochastic observable
algebra estimate: it must control the two-replica tilted expectations or an
adapted likelihood/duality expansion in terms of the uniform degree-D moment
certificates, while retaining Brownian cancellation before summing absolute
spatial coefficients. A bound on expected coefficient-l1 mass alone cannot
provide that interface, as Section 5's deterministic example already shows.
No such adapted estimate is claimed here. Nor is its impossibility claimed.

7. RECEIPT AND CONTINUATION

The concrete restricted objective is complete: arbitrary precommitted
sensor motion now has a dimension-free full-record theorem and an explicit
O(n^(-1/2)) certificate. It removes the fixed spatial-sensor restriction for
this class without a visit-count or time-variation requirement. The earlier
fixed-sensor theorem still covers its separately stated arbitrary feedback
class; neither theorem silently contains the other's entire control class.

No numerical run, new worker, public disclosure, Library operation, or
modification of earlier sources occurred. Native inherited Pro; exact
backend, token usage, financial cost and remaining budget UNKNOWN. Costs
belong to P1 separately from Ultra. Root independently agreed with the
overlap derivation before this source was frozen; a full exact-source
independent audit, if desired, is separate from that discussion.

Exact next scientific issue, not an ongoing background claim: derive the
adapted stochastic observable-algebra/two-replica estimate described in
Section 6, or find an operational counterexample under the actual bounded
energy and admissible common-policy hypotheses. No additional investigation
or allocation is assumed by this source.
